title: Salinas Pliego Rejects 40-Hour Workweek; Threatens to Replace 15,000 People with Machines “That Don’t Ask for Maternity Leave”
author: La Jornada Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by[La Jornada Editorial
Staff](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/la%20redacci%C3%B3n) originally
appeared in the [November 17, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/17/economia/salinas-
pliego-amaga-con-sustituir-empleados-por-maquinas-ante-reformas-laborales),
Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** Ricardo Salinas Pliego expressed his opposition to minimum-
wage increases and the proposal to reduce the workweek to 40 hours in Mexico.
He warned that, in response to these measures, he would replace counter
service staff at his financial institution with automated systems and
artificial intelligence.

In a video posted on X, the chairman of Grupo Salinas described these labor
policies as “incredible stupidity” and called them an “attack on employment”
driven by the government.

> [Post by @JorgeArmandoR_ on
> X](https://x.com/JorgeArmandoR_/status/2122793395529617842)

The businessman explained the volume of operations at his bank, through which,
he claimed, half the remittances arriving in the country are paid out,
equivalent to some 500 million dollars a week, to illustrate the impact of
labor costs on his workforce. In that context, he revealed that **he has
already begun reducing his teller staff**.

“I had 15,000 tellers. Had, buddy,” Salinas Pliego emphasized when asked about
the future of these jobs. Referring to the alternative of automation, he
stated: “I’m going to put in a machine.”

## Machines Operate Without Benefits or Unions, He Argues

To justify replacing workers with technology, the businessman argued that
automated equipment offers an operational advantage over labor rights and
benefits.

> “What does the machine do? Well, a machine works 24/7. It has no labor
> problems, no union, no maternity leave, disability leave, breastfeeding…,”
> he listed in the recording.

He also announced that this process would extend to the implementation of
**robotics connected to artificial intelligence**. According to his argument,
the rising cost of labor would allow the investment in these technologies to
be recouped in less time than initially estimated.

Finally, at one point in the recording, when he even asked that his remarks be
omitted (“don’t put that in the video”), Salinas Pliego insisted that the
labor outlook “is going to get worse every day” for employers, reiterating his
criticism of the country’s labor rights reforms.

In addition, Salinas Pliego confirmed on X that he is traveling in Colombia
and met with President Abelardo de la Espriella to “invest and learn.”
